insight.title: How the Silence Holds Us Together
insight.subtitle: Understanding the invisible architecture of our universe.

sections.text: We look up and see a vast, dark velvet. It feels like an empty room, yet it is full of invisible influence. We often wonder why the stars stay put and why our feet remain pressed to the grass. The answer is not a force, but a gentle, hidden architecture surrounding us.

Imagine a heavy silk sheet stretched tight. If you place a marble there, the fabric curves inward. Space behaves exactly like that. Large stars and small planets sit within this invisible fabric, creating soft dips. We are simply rolling along these curves, caught in a beautiful, permanent dance of light and shadow.

This cosmic design means nothing is truly adrift. Every morning, the sun rises because the earth follows these hidden pathways. We are cradled by the very geometry of the universe. It is a quiet reminder that even in the infinite dark, there is a structure that keeps us home, safe and warm.

news.title: “We Cannot Treat Cancer in Isolation”: UFH Researcher Leads Groundbreaking Study on Cardiovascular Health in Breast Cancer Patients
news.description: What happens to blood pressure during cancer treatment, and what does it mean for the heart? This is the question at the centre of Dr Sekoba Nare’s research.

news.title: RIL shares sink 4%, wiping off Rs 82,000 crore as windfall tax on fuel exports returns
news.description: Reliance Industries shares fell, wiping out more than ₹82,000 crore in market value after the government reinstated windfall taxes on diesel and ATF exports. The move, aimed at boosting domestic supply amid volatile global oil markets, was confirmed by Nirmala Sitharaman, who said higher duties would ensure adequate availability of fuel within the country.

news.title: Oil May Reach $200 If Iran War Extends to June, Macquarie Says
news.description: Oil may hit a record $200 a barrel if the Iran war drags on till June, with the Strait of Hormuz staying shut, Macquarie Group Ltd. said.

news.title: Senate votes to fund much of DHS, minus immigration eno : NPR
news.description: The Senate approved a bill to fund most of the Department of Homeland Security, early Friday. The bill does not fund Immigration and Customs Enforcement, or ICE.
